info.title: sharpn Console API
info.description: What the Console may ask of the Console API. Generated from the Zod schemas in `apps/console-api/src/contract`; edit those, not this.

get.summary: Every Light the Bridge knows about
get.description: Read straight through to the Bridge. Nothing is cached here, so this is what the Bridge said a moment ago and not what the Console API remembers.

200.description: Every Light, in whatever order the Bridge listed it.

401.description: `NOT_AUTHENTICATED` — No session, or one that has expired. Sign in again.

500.description: `GATEWAY_MISCONFIGURED` — The Gateway rejected the Console API's Gateway Token. A deployment fault, and deliberately not a 401: the browser has no credential to fix.

501.description: `BRIDGE_UNSUPPORTED` — The Bridge does not serve this at all — older firmware, or a model that cannot do it. Asking again will not change that.

502.description: `GATEWAY_ERROR` — The Gateway failed in a way nothing here anticipated.

503.description:
`GATEWAY_NOT_PAIRED` — The Gateway is not paired with a Bridge, or its Application Key has been revoked and pairing has to be done again. Somebody has to walk to the Bridge; `detail` carries the Gateway's own instructions.

`BRIDGE_UNREACHABLE` — The Gateway could not reach the Bridge.

`BRIDGE_BUSY` — The Bridge is rate limiting the Gateway. Deliberately not a 429: a 429 from the Console API only ever means the browser is going too fast.

`GATEWAY_UNREACHABLE` — This API could not reach the Gateway at all — the channel is down, or its certificate did not verify.

Retry-After.description: How long to wait before asking again, in seconds. Sent only with the codes on this status that can be waited out; several codes share a status, and most of them cannot.

504.description: `BRIDGE_TIMEOUT` — A read took too long. The Gateway had already retried it, and nothing was changed by asking.

get.description: The Light as the Bridge reports it now. This is the only way to learn what a Light became: an update never answers with one.

patch.description: Answers with an Acknowledgement and never with a Light. A 200 means the exchange completed, which is not the same as the Bridge having done what was asked: it can report a change it made and a refusal about the same request, and `outcome` is how to tell `success` from `partial` and `rejected`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The Light's id, as the Bridge reports it.

200.description: What the Bridge says the Command came to. An `outcome` of `rejected` arrives here rather than as a 4xx: the request was well formed and the Bridge answered it.

400.description:
`INVALID_REQUEST` — The request body is not a Command the Console API can send: a key it does not know, a number out of range, a `null`, or nothing to change.

`COLOR_AND_TEMPERATURE_BOTH_SET` — One command asked for both a colour and a colour temperature. They are a protobuf oneof on the wire, where setting both silently keeps one, so the request is refused rather than half-applied.

`BRIDGE_REJECTED_COMMAND` — The Bridge or the Gateway refused the command, and nothing changed. `detail` says which value it objected to.

401.description: `NOT_AUTHENTICATED` — No session, or one that has expired. Sign in again.

403.description: `CSRF_REJECTED` — A mutation arrived without the CSRF token its session expects.

404.description: `LIGHT_NOT_FOUND` — The Bridge knows no Light with that id.

429.description: `TOO_MANY_REQUESTS` — This browser is going too fast. Reads are not metered.

504.description: `MUTATION_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` — An update took too long, so the Command may have been applied and the reply lost. This is not a failure and must not be reported as one — read the Light to find out what it is now.

LightArchetype.description: What kind of fitting a Light is, spelled the way Hue spells it. `unspecified` is an archetype the Gateway did not recognise, and is not Hue's own `unknown_archetype`.

ColorXy.description: A CIE xy position, as the Bridge reported it.

LightCapabilities.description: What a Light can be told to do. Each flag is the presence of a field on the Bridge's own resource, so a light that cannot be coloured is not a light that is currently black. Read these rather than guessing from the values beside them: a dimmable light may report no brightness.

Light.description: A Light, flat and renamed. The numbers here are whatever the Bridge reported and are not held to the ranges a Command is: a response describes what was seen, where a Command is checked before it is sent.

LightCommand.description: What to change about a Light. Presence is the whole contract: a key this body does not carry never reaches the Bridge, and one it does carry is sent — `false` and `0` included. `null` is refused rather than read as absent, and a body that changes nothing is refused too. Ranges are the Bridge's own; nothing stricter is enforced here.

ResourceIdentifier.description: A Resource the Bridge named, in Hue's own words.

BridgeError.description: What the Bridge refused, in its own words, verbatim.

Acknowledgement.description: What an update did, which is never what a Light now is. It names the Resources the Bridge says it changed and what it refused, and it has nowhere to carry state — read the Light to find out what it became.

ErrorEnvelope.description: Every error, in one shape. `message` is the Console API's own words. `detail` is whoever refused, verbatim — the Gateway's prose, the Bridge's own description, or its own account of what was wrong with the body.

x-correlation-id.description: The Correlation ID this request was logged under. Minted here and never taken from the browser; the same value appears in every error envelope.
